stem: A 6-year-old develops widespread urticaria, facial angioedema, and respiratory difficulty within minutes of eating a suspected allergen. Which statement best fits this presentation?

options.text: This is anaphylaxis and requires urgent treatment
This cannot be anaphylaxis unless hypotension is also present
The size of the skin test is the best predictor of reaction severity
Coexistent asthma does not affect reaction severity
Fish reactions are low risk and predictable

explanation: Anaphylaxis is the correct answer. This acute reaction with skin involvement and respiratory difficulty is consistent with anaphylaxis, which requires urgent treatment.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because this presentation has rapid onset, typical skin features, and respiratory involvement, which fits anaphylaxis and needs urgent treatment
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because hypotension is not required when typical skin features and respiratory compromise are present
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because skin test size predicts the likelihood of reaction, not the severity of future reactions
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because asthma can be a factor associated with more severe reactions
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because fish allergy can be clinically significant and reactions are not simply low risk and predictable
